STEP 1 - Scene: This is a buffet-style plate of Asian finger foods. It holds roast chicken pieces (a thigh/leg quarter), braised soy chicken wings and feet, a braised dark meat item (possibly a duck neck or chicken piece), and a fresh spring roll.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate is a white side/dessert plate with a ribbed rim, about 22 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 11² ≈ 380 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roast chicken quarter
- Braised wing pieces (top)
- Dark braised piece (soy duck or chicken)
- Soy-braised chicken feet / wing tips (left)
- Fresh rice paper roll (shrimp, carrot, herbs)

STEP 4 - Area (food covers about 48% of the plate):
- Roast chicken: 14%
- Top wing pieces: 9%
- Dark braised piece: 7%
- Feet/wings: 9%
- Spring roll: 9%

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Roast chicken: 53 cm² × 3 cm = 160 ml
- Top wing pieces: 34 cm² × 2 cm = 68 ml
- Dark piece: 27 cm² × 2.5 cm = 67 ml
- Feet/wings: 34 cm² × 2 cm = 68 ml
- Spring roll: 34 cm² × 2.5 cm = 85 ml

STEP 6 - Grams. These are bony, gappy pieces, so I used a lower density for most:
- Roast chicken: 160 ml × 0.8 = 128 g
- Top wing pieces: 68 ml × 0.6 = 41 g
- Dark piece: 67 ml × 0.8 = 54 g
- Feet/wings: 68 ml × 0.6 = 41 g
- Spring roll: 85 ml × 0.9 = 77 g

STEP 7 - Energy (edible weight including bone):
- Roast chicken: 128 g × 190 kcal/100 g = 243 kcal
- Top wings: 41 g × 200 = 82 kcal
- Dark piece: 54 g × 220 = 119 kcal
- Feet/wings: 41 g × 200 = 82 kcal
- Spring roll: 77 g × 110 = 85 kcal

Total: about 341 g and 611 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A moderately filled side plate of meat pieces with bones should weigh roughly 340 g, so this total is plausible.
